item.title: Alex Ferguson legacy in focus! Michael Carrick reflects on legendary boss as Manchester United prepare for Aston Villa showdown
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has called on his players to use their midweek European heroics as a springboard for domestic consistency. Speaking ahead of a high-stakes encounter with Aston Villa, the Red Devils boss also took time to reflect on the immense influence of Sir Alex Ferguson as the club marks a major milestone for the legendary Scotsman. Honouring the Ferguson dynasty The atmosphere at Old Trafford this weekend will be charged with nostalgia as Manchester United commemorates 40 years since Sir Alex first walked through the doors of the Theatre of Dreams. Speaking to the media about the legendary manager's enduring impact, Carrick was quick to highlight how the Scotsman's arrival in November 1986 transformed the trajectory of the club forever. "It's something definitely worth celebrating as a football club, 40 years this week since he came here," the United boss explained. "I am probably closer to him, and speak more to him now, than I did when I was playing. Ever since he came here, the impact he has had on me as an individual was immense." To truly honour that history, Carrick believes his side must find the formula for sustained success rather than relying on sporadic bursts of brilliance. Managing the squad after Roma thriller While the focus is partially on the past, Carrick’s immediate concern lies with a squad that is currently balancing the highs of a Champions League comeback with the harsh realities of a growing injury list. The manager confirmed a significant blow to his midfield options, revealing that Carlos Baleba is set for a stint on the sidelines. The youngster suffered an injury during the dramatic 3-2 victory over Roma and is expected to be out for several weeks, with a return only likely following the conclusion of the upcoming international break. There was slightly more optimistic news regarding Patrick Dorgu, who is "slowly getting back" to fitness after a seven-game absence, though his involvement against Villa remains subject to late assessments. Reflecting on the midweek victory that ignited the Old Trafford crowd, Carrick was careful to ensure his players did not become complacent after the emotional high of the European turnaround. He described the result as a "one-off" and stressed that the hard work is only just beginning if the team wants to climb the Premier League table. "We scored some goals from nowhere. I thought we played really well and deserved to win the game. Nothing is done yet. It is one moment in time that we need to use to move forward. We need more of it, for sure," he told the media. I thought we played really well and deserved to win the game. Nothing is done yet. It is one moment in time that we need to use to move forward. We need more of it, for sure," he told the media. Solskjaer support and the path ahead imago-sport-1070999276.jpg The conversation also turned to another former United figure, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who recently spoke to Norwegian media to offer his backing for Carrick to lead the club long-term. Despite the noise surrounding his permanent status in the hotseat, Carrick remained focused on the task at hand, though he spoke warmly of his former colleague and fellow 1999 Treble-winner. The current United boss admitted he had not personally watched the interview but was pleased to hear of the support from a man who understands the unique pressures of the United job better than most. He expressed a desire to see Solskjaer return to management in the near future, describing him as a "fantastic person" who knows him better than almost anyone else in the industry.

item.title: Ravens might be making a huge mistake with new plans for NFL trade deadline
item.description: Ravens might be making a huge mistake with new plans for NFL trade deadline originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens are in trouble. Lamar Jackson is likely out for the rest of the regular season, and Tyler Huntley is as well. They're reportedly trading for Jacoby Brissett, but that might not be enough to salvage the season. With this major quarterback problem, it would not be a surprise if the Ravens adjusted their trade deadline plans. They have made some changes, but it's not exactly how some might've expected after losing QB1 and QB2 for the season in the same game. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Ravens are not planning to sell at this year's trade deadline. Despite their playoff hopes being all but gone, the Ravens are not going to sell, which could wind up being a huge mistake. Ravens could be making a big mistake with plans not to sell at NFL trade deadline "I don't see the Ravens in sell mode," Rapoport said. "The reason why I say that is the Jacoby Brissett trade is going to be official this morning; he is going to be their starting quarterback when they take the field Monday against the Los Angeles Chargers ... So no, I do not believe the Ravens are in sell mode. I don't think they're in buy mode either." From @GMFB: Could the #Ravens be sellers at the trade deadline (no); Plus, the # Vikings will start Carson Wentz on MNF. https://t.co/VAKpk6SThK — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 6, 2026 The Ravens are swinging a trade for Brissett as a temporary resolution to their quarterback problem, but it's hard to believe this team will have much of a chance to win anything this season. Instead, the Ravens should look to trade away players at this year's trade deadline. Losing Jackson and Huntley for the season is a very strong indicator that their season is over. Sure, Brissett might help the Ravens to a win or two throughout the rest of the season. But it's really hard to imagine that this team will be good enough to win anything, especially after how defeated they looked on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. MORE : Why it's time for Colts to move on from Shane Steichen and Daniel Jones The Ravens are now 4-5 on the season, and firmly in last place in the AFC North. Brissett would have to play extremely well for this Ravens team to have any chance of making the playoffs. But even if they did make it there, it's hard to imagine Brissett leading this team on any sort of playoff run. So, with that in mind, the Ravens should really look to sell. They don't have to trade someone like Derrick Henry, as he's in their long-term plans. But players on expiring contracts or veterans who have shaky futures with the team should be readily available. Rashod Bateman, Marlon Humphrey, Chidobe Awuzie, Calais Campbell, Justice Hill, and even someone like Mark Andrews should be available for trade. This season is likely a wash, so the Ravens should be selling. I

item.title: Quinshon Judkins Will Dominate Fantasy for the Next Few Weeks
item.description: Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins runs the ball against the Pittsburgh Steelers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Browns are looking to avenge last week's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, and star running back Quinshon Judkins will play a crucial role in the game-plan this week. Cleveland is set to go on the road to take on the New Orleans Saints, and Judkins is garnering attention as a key contributor for Week 9 fantasy football lineups. He struggled last week against a dominant Steelers front, tallying just 25 rushing yards over 11 carries, adding two catches for 24 yards in the passing game. The week prior, though, Judkins flashed his fantasy ceiling in a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. He posted a season-high 96 rushing yards over 17 carries, taking on encouraging workload near the goal line with two rushing touchdowns for the afternoon. Judkins closed Week 7 ranked as RB3 in PPR for the week, notching a 23.4 fantasy points, another season-high mark. Quinshon Judkins at Titans: 17 CAR 96 YDS 2 TD His third career game with 2+ rush TD. pic.twitter.com/kQQIKKzNzD - StatMuse (@statmuse) October 25, 2026 I expect Judkins will re-capture this caliber of production against New Orleans, and he's building a case to dominate fantasy football for the next few weeks. Quinshon Judkins Will See Expanded Role Alongside Shedeur Sanders Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders hands off the ball to Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Browns are pivoting at the quarterback position, with starter Deshaun Watson set to miss Week 9 due to a concussion. Second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders is set to handle the reins under center for Cleveland, which will likely present expanded volume for Judkins and the run game. Browns QB Deshaun Watson did not practice again Thursday while he remains in concussion protocol; Shedeur Sanders is in line to start Sunday vs. the Saints. - Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 5, 2026 Coming into a favorable matchup against New Orleans, an uptick in workload will help Judkins replicate his RB3 finish from Week 7. He's struggled to carve out consistent efficiency, averaging just 3.4 yards per carry so far this season, but an expanded role should remedy such a concern. Cleveland's offense will feature a steady rushing attack throughout the course of Sunday's game, elevating Judkins' fantasy ceiling heading into a notably favorable matchup. Las Vegas enters its respective Week 9 matchup ranked 31st in run defense, while Cincinnati is ranked as the No. 20 unit against the run. Houston will present a tough matchup, but has struggled at times against the run, allowing 294 rushing yards over its last two games. item.title: The Fifa hopeful hoping to take Infantino down with 'samurai spirit'
item.description: [Getty Images] Kozo Tashima is under no illusions it will be easy to take down Gianni Infantino - but the first serious challenger for the Fifa presidency says he will draw on his "samurai spirit". First, the 68-year-old needs to get the endorsement of five member associations around the world. The honorary president of the Japan Football Association said he has had "good replies" from those he has contacted since announcing his ambition to run in the March elections. If he achieves the necessary endorsements, the next step is an altogether different proposition - toppling Infantino, who has been in charge of Fifa for a decade and told BBC Sport last month he believed he had the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football. Tashima, who sits on the Fifa Council, acknowledged the scale of the challenge, but wants to bring "good change" to the organisation. The former footballer says he is driven by disappointment in Infantino's recent actions, surrounding the cancelled suspension of United States forward Folarin Balogun at the World Cup and the abandoned plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. In an exclusive interview with BBC Sport, he spoke of why he feels he cannot leave Fifa as it is. "I know [Infantino] has a lot of supporters," he said. "Now I am alone and my budget is not enough but it is OK. My policy, my philosophy, I have to fight against him with my samurai spirit. "I would like to make sure that the game of football is safeguarded and to be loved and enjoyed by everybody. We have to review the system in Fifa and build good governance. "In the uncertain situation of the world, sports - especially football - can present good values like fair play, co-operation, hard work, integrity, and show the model of the society. So, first to review and rebuild good governance and make football accessible for all with the principle of football first." Japan's Tashima to stand against Infantino for Fifa presidency Fifa to share 'key documents' over World Cup sell-off plan Infantino says he is backed by 'vast majority' Asked how confident he was in his ability to get the five endorsements, he said: "I have confidence. I already asked to some of the member association and [received] good replies so far." He laughed when asked if he realistically hopes to win the election in Morocco in March, before saying: "Of course, of course yes, I hope I will win. It is not easy." Tashima's campaign will centre on his philosophy for the role of Fifa president, which he described as one based on the "values of sincerity, soundness, fair play, and integrity". So, first to review and rebuild good governance and make football accessible for all with the principle of football first." Japan's Tashima to stand against Infantino for Fifa presidency Fifa to share 'key documents' over World Cup sell-off plan Infantino says he is backed by 'vast majority' Asked how confident he was in his ability to get the five endorsements, he said: "I have confidence. I already asked to some of the member association and [received] good replies so far." Regarding the Balogun red-card incident, which involved US President Donald Trump calling Infantino to ask for the ban to be reviewed, Tashima said: "I have never seen the red card and the next game who can play. "This is, I hope, never happens in the world football. He didn't explain about this issue, how to come and how [it came] to happen. He added: "Most of the things are not answered yet by Mr President Infantino. "With my experience in Japan Football Association, Asian Football Confederation, and Fifa, for some more than 20 years, I would like to bring good change if I am elected." Last month, former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega announced his intention to stand as a candidate in next year's Fifa presidential election. He told BBC Sport he had received "more than five" endorsements, but declined to give details of the identities of the member associations backing him. All candidates must prove they have played an "active role" in football for two of the last five years. Vega has said he is confident he is eligible to stand for the presidency as a shareholder of a club. Vega has attempted to run for the presidency three times before but each time has failed to garner the necessary support of five associations. Tashima can therefore be considered the first serious challenger to Infantino. item.title: Ben Roethlisberger says Steelers RB Jaylen Warren belongs in MVP conversation
item.description: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s hard to put into words just how important Jaylen Warren has been to the Steelers’ success this season. The running back’s 998 scrimmage yards through eight weeks of action is good for third in the league behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. There is no doubt that Warren is playing at an elite level, and people are starting to have some serious conversations about the way the back has been playing. Former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger recently went as far as to say that Warren deserves MVP consideration for his play so far this season on his “Footbahlin with Ben Roethlisberger” podcast. “This guy needs to start to be talked about in some MVP stuff. Like league MVP or offensive MVP,” Roethlisberger said. “His numbers and some of the stuff he’s doing is pretty impressive. His yards after contact have to be some of the highest in the league. There’s a lot of things that don’t look good and then all of a sudden it’s like, oh, he fell forward for three.” Warren is averaging 4.89 yards per touch so far this season, the most by any running back with at least 100 touches. Despite his incredible efficiency and performance this season, there are still 16 players with higher odds to win the NFL’s Offensive Player of the Year award on FanDuel Sportsbook. Is Warren a value play? Possibly, but the clear reason for the lack of love for Warren comes from the fact that he only has three touchdowns this season. Despite being a workhouse and the best player on Pittsburgh’s offense, the touchdown output, coupled with the Steelers not being a flashy offense, hurts his chances significantly. All of this to say that Roethlisberger is absolutely correct in saying Warren deserves significantly more attention than he is getting for the unbelievable season he is in the midst of having for the Steelers. item.title: Arteta confirms Saka out for 'weeks', Konsa fit
item.description: Bukayo Saka will be sidelined for "weeks" by a quad injury (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Mikel Arteta said Friday that Arsenal winger Bukayo Saka would be out of action for "weeks" but had a positive message about the fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and William Saliba. Saka was forced off with a quad injury during Arsenal's 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich last month and was left out of Thomas Tuchel's squad for upcoming England matches. "We're talking about obviously weeks, let's say after the international break," Arsenal boss Arteta said ahead of the visit of Hull to the Emirates Stadium on Saturday. "He's going to start hitting the pitch and start to have more activity and see how he feels, but unfortunately he's going to be out for a while." Konsa was taken off during a 2-1 win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday but is fit to face Hull. The former Aston Villa defender was recruited in August, partly to provide cover for Saliba during his prolonged absence with a back injury. Saliba returned to the squad for the first time this season for the trip to Prague but did not play. Arteta, whose team are top of the Premier League, said he would not stand in the way if coach Zinedine Zidane calls up Saliba to the France squad. "They have all the information. Now it's about them, about Zinedine in this case, to give the call," said Arteta. "We will accept whatever it is. It's more between them because William needs minutes as well." He added: "I know how much he loves to be around the national team. It's a new manager, a really exciting one as well, so whatever he's decided is fine for us." Despite the absence of Saka, Tuchel's squad includes five Arsenal players -- Ben White, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze, Declan Rice and Konsa. item.content:encoded: Bukayo Saka will be sidelined for "weeks" by a quad injury (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Mikel Arteta said Friday that Arsenal winger Bukayo Saka would be out of action for "weeks" but had a positive message about the fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and William Saliba. Saka was forced off with a quad injury during Arsenal's 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich last month and was left out of Thomas Tuchel's squad for upcoming England matches. "We're talking about obviously weeks, let's say after the international break," Arsenal boss Arteta said ahead of the visit of Hull to the Emirates Stadium on Saturday. "He's going to start hitting the pitch and start to have more activity and see how he feels, but unfortunately he's going to be out for a while." Konsa was taken off during a 2-1 win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday but is fit to face Hull. The former Aston Villa defender was recruited in August, partly to provide cover for Saliba during his prolonged absence with a back injury. Saliba returned to the squad for the first time this season for the trip to Prague but did not play. Arteta, whose team are top of the Premier League, said he would not stand in the way if coach Zinedine Zidane calls up Saliba to the France squad. "They have all the information. Now it's about them, about Zinedine in this case, to give the call," said Arteta. "We will accept whatever it is. It's more between them because William needs minutes as well." He added: "I know how much he loves to be around the national team. It's a new manager, a really exciting one as well, so whatever he's decided is fine for us." Despite the absence of Saka, Tuchel's squad includes five Arsenal players -- Ben White, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze, Declan Rice and Konsa. "It is a proud thing to have a big English core in the national team," said Arteta. "Our club, it is something that is part of our identity. They are super happy to be back, you can see that. Let's focus on tomorrow and then after that they can go and do their bit with the national team." kca/jw/gj

item.title: Warriors’ Jimmy Butler’s lively sideline antics vs. Heat draw obvious relationship analogy
item.description: Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images Warriors’ Jimmy Butler’s lively sideline antics vs. Heat draw obvious relationship analogy appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jimmy Butler couldn’t hide his excitement during the Golden State Warriors ’ 120-100 victory over the Miami Heat, and teammate Georges Niang had a hilarious explanation. The injured star, who has been working toward his return from a torn ACL, was particularly animated on the sideline against his former team. Speaking after the win, Niang addressed Butler’s lively behavior, joking that the forward probably had extra motivation against Miami. “I wonder why,” Niang said when asked about Butler’s energy. He then offered a relationship analogy to explain the competitive feelings that can linger after leaving a team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Do you want to see your ex do better than she was with you? Not really.” Niang, who has played for several NBA teams, admitted he understands wanting to prove something against a former organization. He also joked that Butler was probably listening to country music and screaming in the weight room. Beyond the jokes, Niang praised Butler’s character and generosity behind the scenes. He recalled how Butler welcomed teammates to San Diego home and continued checking on them despite his injury. Niang revealed that Butler even offered him help while recovering from his torn ACL, something that genuinely surprised the veteran forward. Butler’s enthusiasm also followed his playful Instagram trolling after the Heat victory, adding another entertaining chapter to his reunion with Miami. Although Butler remains sidelined, Niang’s comments highlighted how the Warriors star continues supporting his teammates while maintaining his trademark humor. His presence has provided Golden State with another source of leadership, showing that Butler remains invested in the team’s success even while facing a lengthy recovery. Related: Warriors’ Draymond Green fires back at Dillon Brooks by calling out ‘de-escalate’ BS after recent skirmish Related: Warriors star Stephen Curry reveals Steve Kerr’s message after 0-3 start that sparked win streak

item.title: Daily Slop: Why Jayden Daniels is next-level protecting the ball (via Washington Post)
item.description: The Daily Slop – 6 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Post (paywall) How Jayden Daniels turned protecting the football into his ‘superpower’ Through all of the Commanders’ struggles, the quarterback has remained one of the NFL’s most efficient passers. Ahead of his freshman year of college in 2019, Jayden Daniels sat down with then-Arizona State coach Herm Edwards. The quarterback had been an excellent decision-maker in high school, but the former NFL coach wanted to drill home that the margin for error was about to shrink. He figured that Daniels had a future playing on Sundays and wanted to prepare him for what would come next. “He always told me, ‘No matter what, you give yourself a chance to win the game if the possession always ends with a kick,’” Daniels told The Washington Post. “Whether that’s a punt or a field goal, you always want to end it with a kick.” That was ingrained in Daniels throughout his five years of college football, and it hasn’t changed in the slightest through his third season with the Washington Commanders. Among the 33 NFL quarterbacks who’ve attempted at least 100 passes this season, he’s the only one who hasn’t committed a turnover. Few quarterbacks have been better than Daniels at protecting the football since he entered the NFL in 2024. He has an interception rate of just 1.5 percent (the fourth lowest among quarterbacks who attempted at least 500 passes during that span). Overall, he’s committed just 14 turnovers (tied for the fewest). “You just got to be locked in for six seconds each play,” Daniels said. “It kind of just goes with the flow of the game. And then, also, just having that discipline of like, ‘Okay, if it’s not there, don’t force it.’” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders Mailbag: Is Luke McCaffrey Being Overlooked? Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Post (paywall) How Jayden Daniels turned protecting the football into his ‘superpower’ Through all of the Commanders’ struggles, the quarterback has remained one of the NFL’s most efficient passers. Ahead of his freshman year of college in 2019, Jayden Daniels sat down with then-Arizona State coach Herm Edwards. The quarterback had been an excellent decision-maker in high school, but the former NFL coach wanted to drill home that the margin for error was about to shrink. He figured that Daniels had a future playing on Sundays and wanted to prepare him for what would come next. “He always told me, ‘No matter what, you give yourself a chance to win the game if the possession always ends with a kick,’” Daniels told The Washington Post. “Whether that’s a punt or a field goal, you always want to end it with a kick.” That was ingrained in Daniels throughout his five years of college football, and it hasn’t changed in the slightest through his third season with the Washington Commanders. Among the 33 NFL quarterbacks who’ve attempted at least 100 passes this season, he’s the only one who hasn’t committed a turnover. Few quarterbacks have been better than Daniels at protecting the football since he entered the NFL in 2024. He has an interception rate of just 1.5 percent (the fourth lowest among quarterbacks who attempted at least 500 passes during that span). Overall, he’s committed just 14 turnovers (tied for the fewest). “You just got to be locked in for six seconds each play,” Daniels said. “It kind of just goes with the flow of the game. And then, also, just having that discipline of like, ‘Okay, if it’s not there, don’t force it.’” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders Mailbag: Is Luke McCaffrey Being Overlooked? Did Dan Quinn Win Back Trust? With Terry McLaurin out for the year, McCaffrey’s limited role on offense is harder to overlook. Plus, what the Eagles win did—and didn’t—change for Dan Quinn. Luke McCaffrey looked good on that long kickoff return, but he barely played on offense. With Terry out for the year, is there a reason he still isn’t getting more opportunities at receiver? Question from Nigel F. via email That’s a great question that I’ve written about here before . From what I can tell, the staff likes McCaffrey, or he wouldn’t be on the roster, but he somehow keeps falling outside of the group that gets the main share of the offensive snaps at receiver. Against Philadelphia, McCaffrey played just three offensive snaps. Antonio Williams played 50, Treylon Burks 40, and Stefon Diggs 39. The team loaded up at receiver this offseason, giving the staff options even after McLaurin went down. The receiver room may not be big on names outside of McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, but rookie Antonio Williams is emerging fast , and whenever Treylon Burks can stay healthy, he routinely produces. Add in the attention tight end Chig Okonkwo gets, and there’s not much left for McCaffrey, Dyami Brown, or Van Jefferson. On film, McCaffrey gets open, so offensive coordinator David Blough has to make the scheme work with the talent they have. With injuries playing a factor, McCaffrey will likely get his shot to show what he brings to the field before the end of the season. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Commanders’ grand offensive transformation remains a work in progress The Washington Commanders didn’t start over completely after their 2025 season ended with only a handful of wins. A month after the team moved on from its previous coordinators, coach Dan Quinn reintroduced David Blough, previously the assistant quarterbacks coach, as his new play caller and they laid out their basic vision of the offense. Blough’s would be “an aggressive, balanced attack,” Quinn said, with more under-center formations and a departure from the no-huddle system Jayden Daniels had grown accustomed to over the past two years. It would require the young quarterback to get comfortable with relaying play calls — some of them lengthy — then quickly reading the defense to make any checks at the line of scrimmage. Among the more noticeable changes: Daniels would work under center more and no longer operate almost exclusively from the shotgun formation. “I think it opens up some different schemes in the run game, some things that I believe in,” Blough explained in February. “It opens up different play actions and keepers and getting him on the perimeter in different ways. I think there’s a level of communication that happens under center. … I think a lot of teams that you saw even playing deep into the playoffs, it was something that was a foundation of what they did.” The goal, both Quinn and Blough said, was to create a more explosive system that would take advantage of Daniels’ accuracy and running without asking him to do everything for the offense. Throughout the offseason, Blough, a first-time play caller, collaborated with his assistants and sought the input of his players as they built a system they said would be exclusively theirs. The foundation was an amalgamation of the offenses Blough ran during his years as a quarterback, and drawing from the offenses run by Washington’s previous play caller, Kliff Kingsbury, as well as Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell and even Louisville coach Jeff Brohm, whom Blough played for at Purdue. The crux of the Commanders’ offense, however, would draw from Ben Johnson, Blough’s former coordinator in Detroit who has since transformed the Chicago Bears’ offense with his heavy use of play action, multiple tight end sets, outside zone run concepts and pre-snap motion. To read more of this story, click here Last Man Standig (paywall) OFF SCRIPT: Austin Ekeler wasn’t sure he’d play again. He was OK with that. The Commanders running back opens up about nearly retiring after tearing his Achilles, AI’s upside and scary possibilities, growing up in rural Colorado and the NFL statistic he treasures most. ASHBURN, Va. — Austin Ekeler thought he had reached the finish line of his playing career. Not necessarily while lying on the Lambeau Field grass in pain after tearing his right Achilles. But soon after the non-contact injury in Week 2 that ended his 2025 season, any quiet time became a mental battle. “I’m probably done,” Ekeler thought. “Probably retiring.” The entire picture of his work and life put the injury into perspective. The running back was a workhorse for much of his seven-year stint with the Chargers. He helped the Washington Commanders reach the NFC Championship Game in season 8. Then Ekeler tore his Achilles in Year 9. He would be 31 if he returned. 2025 was also the first year he became a father. Ekeler and his wife, Melanie, welcomed a baby boy into the world that May. The guy who grew up on a farm in rural Northern Colorado was already busy “ripping projects,” from coding to creating apps to business and real estate investing. He loves football, but it’s not his life. And yet… “I told myself, ‘Look, let’s focus on the rehab. Don’t focus on whether I’m done or not. Don’t make that decision while I’m emotional. Continue to rehab, and then once that’s done, let’s get back in shape.” Ekeler is a gym guy, so he would get back into shape regardless. “Then, if I start to feel good and people are calling about me, I’ll do a workout. If they want to have me in, great. If not, let’s go rip some more code and build some more projects. That’s what it was for me.” The calls did come. The Carolina Panthers checked in and were set to add Ekeler to their practice squad when Washington raised the stakes with a spot on the active roster. For more from

item.title: Braves Must Fix Shortstop Hole Before Vegas Meetings Start
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect The Atlanta Braves season is over, but the real work starts right now with a glaring hole at shortstop. Battery Power reported on November 5 that the team needs a new shortstop and asked fans if any options catch their eye. This isn’t a minor fix; it is the single biggest move the front office must make before the season begins again. The roster has gaps, and the clock is already ticking on the free agent market. While the team figures out the lineup, they have secured stability on the dugout bench. Battery Power noted on November 4 that the Braves set to return their entire coaching staff for 2027. Keeping the same coaches gives the players a solid base to build on while the front office hunts for new bats and arms. This continuity matters more than people think when you are trying to win a division title. The Shortstop Void The need at shortstop is the most urgent issue facing the franchise. Battery Power listed several options and asked fans to weigh in on who they want to see in the lineup. The team cannot win a championship with a weak spot in the middle of the diamond. They need a player who can hit and field at an elite level. The options are out there, but the Braves must act fast to get the best one. Prospects like Tate Southisene and Briggs McKenzie are making waves in the Arizona Fall League. Battery Power reported that both players made the AFL Fall Stars Game, which shows the farm system has depth. However, the major league team cannot wait for kids to be ready if they want to win now. The big league roster needs an immediate upgrade, not a hope for the future. Awards and Money Talk The offseason comes with plenty of awards to hand out and money to discuss. Battery Power mentioned that the Rookie of the Year announcement drops on November 9, and Didier Fuentes likely will not win. The Manager of the Year vote comes on November 10, with Matty Mattingly, Pat Weiss, and Craig Murphy as the top names. These awards are fun to talk about, but they do not put runs on the board. Financial reports also came out ahead of a potential lockout. The Braves released their third quarter 2026 financial reports, and the numbers show the team is ready to spend. Salary cap and floor rules are always a hot topic for fans. The front office has the money to fix the shortstop spot, so there is no excuse for them to sit on their hands. What Happens in Vegas The real action starts next week when the MLB General Manager Meetings kick off on November 9 in Las Vegas. Battery Power reported that these meetings usually set the groundwork for trades and free agent evaluations. A small chance exists for minor additions to happen right then, but the big deals will start here. The Braves need to be aggressive in the room to get the player they need.

item.title: Why Omarion Miller's breakout game for ASU could come against former team
item.description: Towards the end of practice on Nov. 3, right after Arizona State senior wide receiver Omarion Miller finished talking to local reporters, there was a fun moment between Miller and his teammate, senior safety Adrian “Boogie” Wilson. Wilson is one of the more lively characters on the roster, and this moment was an example of that. Pretending to be a reporter himself, Wilson began to ask Miller questions ahead of this weekend’s home game against Colorado on Nov. 7 . The first one was in jest, with Wilson asking, ‘Who is your favorite teammate?’ Miller responded, ‘Probably Boogie Wilson.’ Then Wilson got into the meat of his questions. “‘What’re you most excited for playing your former team?’” Miller responded quickly. “‘To beat ‘em real bad.’” The answer was short but came with conviction. Miller is set to go against the same team he suited up for from 2023 to 2025. While Miller did his best not to provide Colorado with bulletin board material, it’s only natural to feel more pressure going against your former team. “You're going to feel something, right?” coach Kenny Dillingham said. “People are going to take that and potentially twist that. They twist everything. But you can't say no. But you can't say yes. Every person is going to handle things different. “I know he's been the same guy this week for us, same attitude, same everything. You wouldn't know the difference. But there has to be something in your head, right? That's human nature.” Miller still has a bunch of friends that he keeps in contact with in Boulder, but not for this week. It’s a place where Miller saw himself grow up, maturing into a leader for younger players in his time with the Buffaloes. “Man, I ain't gonna lie, this week I'm pretty excited going against my old team,” Miller said. “A lot of emotions going on right now, for sure. I played there for three years, going against my former team; those were my guys. Anxious to get on the field and ball.” And ball he might. It’s been an up-and-down season for Miller, who started off with eight receptions for 102 yards and one touchdown in the season opener — but that was against lower-level competition, FCS Morgan State. Miller, a priority target in the transfer portal for ASU, recorded five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown against Baylor, although that came in a 55-19 blowout loss, one of the worst of the Dillingham era. Miller just broke a three-game spell without a touchdown by hauling in a 20-yard score to cut the lead to 17-10 against BYU on Oct. 31. The first one was in jest, with Wilson asking, ‘Who is your favorite teammate?’ Miller responded, ‘Probably Boogie Wilson.’ Then Wilson got into the meat of his questions. “‘What’re you most excited for playing your former team?’” Miller responded quickly. “‘To beat ‘em real bad.’” The answer was short but came with conviction. While Miller did his best not to provide Colorado with bulletin board material, it’s only natural to feel more pressure going against your former team. “You're going to feel something, right?” coach Kenny Dillingham said. “People are going to take that and potentially twist that. They twist everything. But you can't say no. But you can't say yes. Every person is going to handle things different. “I know he's been the same guy this week for us, same attitude, same everything. You wouldn't know the difference. But there has to be something in your head, right? That's human nature.” Miller still has a bunch of friends that he keeps in contact with in Boulder, but not for this week. It’s a place where Miller saw himself grow up, maturing into a leader for younger players in his time with the Buffaloes. “Man, I ain't gonna lie, this week I'm pretty excited going against my old team,” Miller said. “A lot of emotions going on right now, for sure. I played there for three years, going against my former team; those were my guys. Anxious to get on the field and ball.” And ball he might. It’s been an up-and-down season for Miller, who started off with eight receptions for 102 yards and one touchdown in the season opener — but that was against lower-level competition, FCS Morgan State. Miller, a priority target in the transfer portal for ASU, recorded five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown against Baylor, although that came in a 55-19 blowout loss, one of the worst of the Dillingham era. Miller just broke a three-game spell without a touchdown by hauling in a 20-yard score to cut the lead to 17-10 against BYU on Oct. 31. The senior wide receiver feels like he’s on the verge of a breakout game — “Most definitely,” he said with a smile — and so do his coaches. “It's close,” Dillingham said. “Last week there were multiple opportunities that (if) one of those balls is caught, that's his breakout game. There it is, just one of those four or five other opportunities. It's going to happen. It's just a matter of when, because we're all around it, we're dancing with it.” Heading into the season, Miller and fellow transfer Reed Harris, coming over from Boston College, knew it was unlikely they were both going to have huge seasons. So far, it’s been Harris (48 receptions for 804 yards and eight touchdowns) who has broken out and is gaining traction as a first-round NFL draft pick. “Coming here, both of us knew we both couldn't be the guys,” Miller said. “So we knew one of us was gonna have to be lower than the other one.” Scouting report: How Arizona State football and Jake Fette can beat Colorado Many thought it would be Miller, who was ranked No. 2 in the transfer portal among wide receivers. But Miller has taken it all in stride and is happy for his teammate. Miller said that probably wouldn’t have been the case a few years ago. “As a young guy, I probably would not be happy,” Miller said. “That's part of learning as a college player. When it’s all said and done, we’re a team. I’m always happy for any one of my teammates. Whether they're doing good or bad, I stay motivated now, and they stay motivating me. We stay on each other so we can all do our best.” Defenses are starting to zero in on Harris, with BYU sending a safety at Harris at the start of each snap for most of the game. Miller is hoping to use that to his advantage. “They just want to double Reed,” Miller said. “They forgot I'm still on the team.” It’s been a quarterback carousel for ASU this season, with freshman Jake Fette now helming the offense after sophomore Cutter Boley began the year as the starter and then was replaced by senior Mikey Keene. A knee injury to Keene paved the path for Fette. While it’s early on, Miller can feel the connection between him and Fette growing. “It’s coming along really good,” Miller said. “I feel like Jake knows the skill set of our receivers. I always tell him, ‘Throw it in the air, and we gonna make you look good.’” Miller’s on the cusp of showing why the Sun Devils targeted him so quickly in the transfer portal, and it may poetically come against the team he left for ASU. item.title: Will Falcons’ James Pearce Jr. play vs. Bengals in Week 9 after 8-game suspension?
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Will Falcons’ James Pearce Jr. play vs. Bengals in Week 9 after 8-game suspension? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Falcons will be playing against the Cincinnati Bengals this week, and there is a chance one of their players won’t be on the field. After serving an eight-game suspension, James Pearce Jr . was eligible to return this week, but he’s also dealing with a back injury that the team is monitoring, according to team reporter Tori McElhaney. “A change to the injury report: RB Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) has been ruled OUT. James Pearce Jr. is dealing with a back issue that the Falcons will monitor throughout the weekend, per Kevin Stefanski,” McElhaney wrote on X, formerly Twitter. The Falcons are hoping that they can get Pearce back so they can get a boost on the defensive end, specifically getting pressure on the quarterback. They’ve been fine at doing so throughout the season, but Pearce brings another level that they can help them become even better in that category. He showed that last season in his rookie year when he finished with 10 1/2 sacks. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I see it as a positive to add a good player to the mix,” Stefanski said via Daniel Fick of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution. “I think the way ‘Brick’ and the defensive staff have constructed this rush plan, obviously married up with the coverage plan, I think it’s beneficial to all parties to do your job. But adding another good player to the mix is a good thing.” James was suspended for eight games for violating the league’s personal conduct policy after he was arrested in February due to an altercation with his ex-girlfriend. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons had a debut that will be remembered for years to come as he stifled the Seahawks offense for much of the game. item.content:encoded: There is arguably no team in the NFL hotter right now than the Chicago Bears , and fans are in for another prime-time showdown this weekend as they get set to welcome the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to town for Sunday Night Football. The Bears (6-2) are winners of three in a row after they traveled to the Pacific Northwest and defeated the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17 in one of the best regular season victories in recent memory. Quarterback Caleb Williams was able to move the ball unlike previous quarterbacks against Seattle's defense, while running back D'Andre Swift capitalized with three rushing touchdowns. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons had a debut that will be remembered for years to come as he stifled the Seahawks offense for much of the game. As for the Buccaneers (3-5), they have climbed their way out of the NFC South basement and are back on tracking following the return of quarterback Baker Mayfield. Tampa has won three of their last four games and is coming off a historic 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons, where they didn't complete a single pass in monsoon conditions. Despite their poor record, the Buccaneers have a formidable defense, and their offense can get things going with their impressive ground attack. Here are five Buccaneers players we'll be watching this Sunday night: 1. QB Baker Mayfield It's been two weeks since Baker Mayfield returned to action following an injury to his right hand, and he hasn't had to do a whole lot. During Tampa Bay's two-game winning streak, Mayfield has completed just seven of 14 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown. He made history last week by not completing a single pass in the Buccaneers' win over the Falcons, which is a nice soft restart to his season. Don't expect that to be the case Sunday, though. The Bears' defense will be too good to allow Tampa to solely rely on their rushing attack to carry the load. Mayfield will likely have his most passing attempts since late September against a Bears defense that can suddenly now get after the quarterback more effectively. We'll see how healed his thumb is and whether or not he can get after this Bears secondary that has a proponent for giving up big passing plays. 2. RB Bucky Irving If the Bears are going to stifle the Buccaneers offense, they need to contain running back Bucky Irving. And this is a homecoming Irving is likely looking forward to. The 2024 fourth-round pick out of Hazel Crest is playing in his first game in Chicago since turning pro, and he's coming off a career day. Irving totaled 170 rushing yards on 27 carries last week and scored a touchdown in Tampa's win over Atlanta. The rushing yards and carries were both career highs, and it was Irving's third game in four weeks with over 100 rushing yards. He is the engine that is powering the Buccaneers' offense and will be the focal point that the defense needs to hone in on. Irving could have a long day, though, considering the Bears' defense hasn't allowed 100 yards rushing in a game since Week 3 and is allowing the fourth-fewest yards per game (86.8). 3. C Graham Barton A big reason the Buccaneers' run offense has been so effective as of late has been because of Graham Barton's improved play. The third-year center has been one of the better centers as of late, becoming a problem for opposing defensive lines. He was hitting key blocks all day long against the Falcons to help the Buccaneers rush for 324 yards, and he did so while battling the flu. Barton will likely be much closer to 100% this weekend, and the Buccaneers will need him to be. He'll be squaring off against Jeffery Simmons, who terrorized the Seahawks offensive line just a few days ago. The Buccaneers offensive line as a whole is strong with Tristan Wirfs and Luke Goedeke anchoring the tackle positions, but Barton's level of play has taken them to a new level. It will be interesting to see how he handles an improved Bears defensive line. 4. DE Reuben Bain If you asked 10 Bears fans who they were hoping to land in the 2026 NFL Draft, the vast majority would have said defensive end Reuben Bain, fully knowing there was little to no shot he would be available to them at pick No. 25. They will get to see him in action, though, as one of Tampa's edge rushers, and he faces a tall task in going against Darnell Wright. Bain, the No. 15 overall pick in the draft, had a slow start to his NFL career but has picked things up in recent weeks. Over his last three games, Bain has totaled one sack, one tackle for loss, and seven pressures. Bain is a smaller edge rusher, and concerns about his arm length were prevalent throughout the pre-draft process. Those concerns could come into play against Wright, who is a hulking right tackle and has allowed just 12 pressures and one sack all year. 5. LB Alex Anzalone Bears fans know Alex Anzalone all too well from his days with the Detroit Lions. The veteran linebacker left Detroit in the offseason for Tampa Bay and was having a quiet season before breaking out for a career day last Sunday. Anzalone was responsible for two of Falcons quarterback Michael Penix's four interceptions, both coming in the first quarter. That put him to three on the year, which nearly matches his career total coming into the season (four). While it's highly unlikely Anzalone has a repeat performance against a quarterback that has thrown just 14 interceptions in two and a half seasons, his familiarity with the Bears and head coach Ben Johnson could prove useful for the Buccaneers defense. Anzalone only went up against the Bears once last season when he was with the Lions, and that was back in Week 2. Much has changed since then. He will be the field general for the defense and try to counteract Williams, something that is becoming increasingly more difficult for defenders. item.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Nottingham Forest’s historic goal drought at home is part of longstanding problem
item.description: Oliver Glasner’s side are yet to score at City Ground this season but troubles in front of goal precede his arrival Nottingham Forest and Schalke are yet to score at home in 2026-27. The former are one of only five teams in the history of the English top flight to have failed to score in their first four home league matches. Three of the preceding four also drew a blank in game five, which will be deflating news for Oliver Glasner with Manchester City heading to the City Ground on Saturday looking for a win after consecutive league defeats. Forest’s expected goals total implies they should have scored but a flaw in their data shows a reason why. They also failed to find the net in a Carabao Cup home game with Leeds, meaning they have amassed 70 shots in all competitions without giving the home fans a goal to celebrate. As extreme as this situation has become, Forest scored only two goals more than the lowest home scorers in the Premier League last season (Burnley), drawing a blank on nine occasions. This is a longstanding issue. Continue reading...

item.title: Win at Everton would put Coventry on right side of history in survival fight
item.description: None of the 21 sides who had 12 points after 10 matches, over the past decade, were relegated from the Premier League If Coventry win at Everton on Friday night they will take an enormous stride towards maintaining their Premier League status. That might seem a huge statement with 28 games remaining, but victory would put Frank Lampard’s side on the right side of recent history. For now, they stand on a precipice. Coventry have taken nine points from nine league matches. Eight teams in the previous 10 seasons were in the same position – seven stayed up. The exception, Leicester in 2024-25, were newly promoted and have tumbled downwards ever since. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Lampard appreciation at Everton, Glasner sparking Forest fire, Zubimendi and Kroupi in spotlight and Carrick v Emery Premier League top scorers Nothing better encapsulates the dysfunction that was Everton under Farhad Moshiri than the idea that an unknown vandal with a can of spray paint could influence the club’s managerial direction. “Pereira out, Lampard in” they daubed on a wall at Goodison Park when it appeared Vítor Pereira was in line to replace Rafael Benítez in 2022. Alarmed by fan protests, the Everton board opted instead for Frank Lampard and, while his tenure ended 12 months later with the club immersed in another relegation battle, there will be appreciation for the Coventry manager when he makes a first visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday. The connection between Lampard and Evertonians was genuine and a factor in keeping the club up in 2022. Both parties will be glad to see the other emerging stronger from those troubled times. Jack Grealish, meanwhile, will again be absent for Everton after his recent disciplinary breach, although the manager, David Moyes, said: “We will be working again with Jack soon.” Andy Hunter Everton v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times GMT) Leeds v Tottenham, Saturday 12.30pm Continue reading...

item.title: Scott Parker’s dramatic West Ham return leaves him struggling for words
item.description: The former midfielder with impressive managerial promotion record began with a thrilling comeback in draw at Cardiff Three days in and Scott Parker has already lost his voice. West Ham’s head coach arrived on Tuesday, watched his side fight back from 3-0 down to draw with Cardiff on Wednesday and was struggling to make himself heard when he met the media on Thursday afternoon. “It’s like in the summer holidays,” Parker said. “You put the flip-flops on for five weeks, then you come back home and you get your shoes on. You’re in a minute, you’ve got a blister on the back of your heel. It’s the same with a throat. I’ve not shouted for a little while. All of a sudden there’s shouting and it’s a bit croaky.” Continue reading...

item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Football Daily | Como turn on the style and hammer nine past out-of-focus Lens
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! A consistent criticism levelled at Como is that they are simply not “Italian” enough to be a bona fide Serie A club. Bankrolled by an Indonesian ciggy manufacturer, their president has helpfully likened their multi-hubbed business model to that of the Walt Disney Company. In Cesc Fàbregas they have a Spanish coach and their starting XI against Lens in Bigger Cup on Wednesday didn’t feature a single Italian. To add insult to injury, they also thrashed their hosts 9-1 in a show of outright vulgarity that will have had Serie A traditionalists gesticulating angrily. Piling on the hurt against already-humiliated opposition has never been the Italian way, unless both teams have formally agreed to it before the game kicks off. Continue reading...

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
item.description: Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier. Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘She can do what Beckham did’: Océane Hurtré making waves at Birmingham
item.description: WSL’s second-highest goalscorer is likened to England legend for her crossing and has earned France call-up At the conclusion of Birmingham’s warm-up, the players quietly and carefully placed their footballs into a draw-string bag. All except one, Océane Hurtré, who nonchalantly chipped hers straight into the bag from about 15 yards. It was an innocuous moment that might have escaped most onlookers at Hednesford Town’s Keys Park but it demonstrated the swagger with which she is playing. To observe the 22-year-old warming up before the 1-1 League Cup draw at Aston Villa last week was to witness a player making skills look easy, taking one touch where others took two and pulling off no-look passes. She is backing up that panache in the Women’s Super League, as the joint second-highest goalscorer with six from the promoted side’s opening eight matches. Only Khadija Shaw has scored more. Continue reading...

item.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. That very respectable time has now been surpassed by the Premier League’s record appearance maker, so we thought we had better take a gulp of our isotonic energy drink and run through a few more tales of football’s marathon men and women. Continue reading...

item.title: Choke of the century? Chengdu collapse sets up thrilling Chinese Super League climax
item.description: John Aloisi’s players need a point on the final day to seal their maiden title – but their form has dropped off a cliff With four games of the Chinese Super League to go, Chengdu Rongcheng needed just a point to clinch their first title. With one game to go, they still need a point. What was a formality has become a formidable task. The biggest bottle job in Asian football history is very much on and it would be as popular as it would be dramatic. The coach of the Sichuan club, the former Portsmouth and Coventry striker John Aloisi, has seen a 12-point lead over Dalian Yingbo cut to just three before Sunday’s showdowns. Whatever happens, this is a positive and thrilling end to a season that started negatively – literally – with nine of the 16 top-tier clubs kicking off on minus points. Continue reading...

item.title: Mainoo and Lacey raise the spirits but systemic change still required at Manchester United | Nick Ames
item.description: There were protests at Old Trafford and even though two academy products stood out, Michael Carrick’s future is far from safe Green and yellow balloons bobbed around the Stretford End. Tennis balls rained down on the pitch in protest at the chronic, enduringly cinematic decline presided over by Manchester United’s ownership. Then came a reminder of the humble football’s extraordinary power to bend history, minds and wills. United’s players departed victorious having somehow won the game within the game, separating themselves from the fog of unhappy context swirling on all sides and turning the second half into its own soaring, ripping story for the ages. Will it be enough to save Michael Carrick, who was once again serenaded when minds wandered from the joint scourges of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe? If Aston Villa defend a shade more competently than Roma on Sunday then perhaps not. United have led their supporters, remarkable in their tenor of backing for players and head coach here, up more than enough false peaks over the past 13 years. Arguably, that is one reason for Carrick being given the job on a permanent basis. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘An absolute afterthought’: the story of the Nigeria women’s team’s fall from grace
item.description: The Super Falcons won’t be at the World Cup and with the prize money going up, they risk being left even further behind It was a historic result in Casablanca – but not in a good way. Nigeria’s 2-1 defeat against South Africa in a playoff in August meant that the Super Falcons are missing out on the World Cup for the first time. It is a crushing blow for the most decorated national side in Africa across both men and women, one that has won no fewer than 10 Wafcon titles . The journalist and lecturer Dr Victor Ademola was in Morocco the day of the defeat. “It was a very difficult evening,” he says. “Some players were visibly emotional while others appeared to be processing what had just happened. I saw players crying as they got on to the team bus while some sat alone or remained on their phones, looking very sad.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Aston Villa, ‘unacceptable insults’ and thin-skinned clutching of pearls
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! When Jamie Carragher appeared as a pundit on Sky Sports Super Sunday, Football Daily was surprised he didn’t have a solicitor sitting alongside him, occasionally jotting notes on a pad or leaning over to give whispered instructions and answer “no comment” to any leading questions about Trey Nyoni starting ahead of Ryan Gravenberch. On Friday night, the former Liverpool defender was subjected to a threat of legal action from Aston Villa, who took such grave exception to some “unacceptable insults” he had rained down on them from his podcast pulpit, that they were ready to call in the heavy legal artillery and stop him from preventing their “ascension in English and European football”. Taking a leaf out of the tried-and-much-ridiculed Nottingham Forest playbook , Villa chair Nassef Sawiris appears to have eschewed contacting Carragher through the usual formal channels and instead cajoled some unfortunate junior comms staffer to make the portentous announcement on their Social Media Disgraces. Continue reading...

item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Marco Rose’s tactics are lifting Bournemouth, Roméo Lavia makes progress with Chelsea and Roberto De Zerbi gives youth a chance at Spurs Good defending is the mark of champions. At Anfield, where Arsenal had not won in the past 13 visits, Mikel Arteta followed the orthodoxy of locking down once his team took the lead. This time around, it proved successful. Arsenal did not allow the occasion or the stadium to get to them as they have on previous occasions. In April 2023, Granit Xhaka entangling with Trent Alexander-Arnold energised home fans previously despondent that Arsenal were 2-0 up. It finished 2-2. On Sunday, Liverpool zipped around zestfully, as Andoni Iraola requests, though the final-ball quality was lacking. That owed a great deal to the organisation of the Arsenal defence. Ahead of the last international break, Brighton set a blueprint for getting the better of Arsenal in winning 3-0 . Liverpool’s squad profile might have made a similar strategy possible though Iraola’s outfit is struggling to create chances in the same volume as Brighton or his Bournemouth team. item.title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Barney Ronay
item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. Continue reading...

item.title: Roster rifts, police raids and Son’s uncertain future leave South Korea at a crossroads
item.description: After a disaster World Cup, the team have continued to spiral, with tensions high between young and older players and the captain’s standing in question Son Heung-min and Cristiano Ronaldo are iconic No 7s, Premier League legends and international record-breakers. Now there is a surprising danger of them having something else in common: being a divisive presence in their national teams. On 21 October, during a parliamentary committee meeting, politician Jeong Yeon-wook put a question to acting Korea Football Association (KFA) president Lee Yong-soo, that took a story out of the sports pages and into the national conversation. “It is said that recently, within the national team squad, players have been calling him not by his name but as ‘No 7’ or ‘that person’. Do you know who that is?” Lee then replied, “Are you referring to Son Heung-min?” Jeong went on: “So it appears to be true. … It has also been revealed that the national team’s leadership is causing discord and has broken down overall.” Lee declined to comment. Continue reading...

item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. Continue reading...

item.title: Kylian Mbappé’s China crisis shows how sensitive Mao’s legacy remains | Rebecca Bailey
item.description: Real Madrid forward was dropped by brands for comments Chinese media generally steered clear of outlining It’s been a bad start to the week for the Kylian Mbappé. The France forward missed out on joining the elite roster of Ballon d’Or winners and instead became the latest high-profile addition to a far less illustrious list – that of foreign brands and individuals charged with “hurting the feelings of the Chinese people”. The saga began when a video of the Real Madrid player making light of a meme involving him and China’s former leader Mao Zedong began spreading. Continue reading...

item.title: Lise Klaveness: ‘Certainly there are people that can challenge Infantino’
item.description: Norwegian federation president distances self from Fifa presidency but believes governing body can be reformed As the rain whips around Oslo’s government quarter, Lise Klaveness is shielding herself from the wind, trying to work out tactics. “Of course we cannot probably do everything alone, but we have a voice, we have the right to speak, we have the right to suggest, so let’s see,” she says. “We will at least try to be a spearhead.” The president of the Norwegian Football Federation wants to re-engage Fifa, and other governing bodies, on the topic of remedy. A slightly arcane aspect of human rights policy in normal times, the importance of remedy became very clear in the aftermath of the World Cup in Qatar, when the families of those injured or killed in the work that led up to the tournament were left without financial compensation after Fifa chose to direct a legacy fund elsewhere. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...
